method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of universality and coded-input arity, with exact formula, macro and reference parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Existence and defining formula of the universal partial computable function, effective enumeration and encoded multi-input functions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: There is a partial computable binary Un such that every unary partial computable f has some natural index e with f(x) partially equal to Un(e,x) for every x. Defining Un via Kleene's T/U normal form proves the theorem.
samples.checks: The existential e follows each f, equality is partial for every x, and the exact displayed T/U formula and cross-reference are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The sequence f_0,f_1,... effectively enumerates every partial computable function and its evaluator is uniform in e and x. Coding number sequences generalizes from unary functions to more inputs. If f is a three-place partial recursive function, decoding a single input x into three components yields a unary partial recursive g.
samples.checks: Universality and uniformity are distinct, binary-versus-unary arity is explicit, and OLCMP-014 keeps the possible undefinedness of g rather than implying totality.

source_observations: OLCMP-014 documents an omitted partial qualifier in the frozen unary-coded example. The target changes only explanatory prose; protected formulas remain exact.
T324 supports the established partial-computability compound, while the universal property and code construction come from OpenLogic.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
